children: Life insurance stocks have been under pressure this year, but improving business momentum is beginning to offer investors a reason to take another look at the sector. August brought a sharp pickup in premium growth, while valuations have also moderated from their historical averages, keeping analysts bullish on the sector for the next leg of re-rating.
So far this year, shares of LIC, HDFC Life, SBI Life, and ICICI Pru Life are down in the range of 4-30 percent.

"At current prices, we are positive on most of the life insurance companies. Our top bet is LIC while on the private side, we are optimistic on HDFC Life and ICICI Prudential Life," said Sharad Avasthi, Head of Research (PCG) at SMIFS.

Analysts at Motilal Oswal expect growth momentum to remain stable in the sector supported by a continued focus on traditional products, better affordability following GST exemptions and wider geographical expansion by private insurers. It prefers SBI Life and LIC.

Similarly, analysts at Antique Stock Broking expect private insurers to sustain mid-teens growth in retail WRP over the medium term and sees favourable risk-reward, with structural growth drivers still intact. It, however, flags regulatory changes around bancassurance and distributor commissions as key risks.
Valuations offer some comfort

The recent correction has brought valuations below their longer-term averages for most major insurers. SBI Life is trading at around 66 times one-year forward earnings versus its five-year average of 77 times. HDFC Life trades at 58 times versus 86 times historically, while ICICI Prudential Life is at 45 times compared with a five-year average of 50 times.
LIC stands out, trading at around 9 times forward earnings against its five-year average of 24 times.

The valuation gap suggests that a significant part of the recent concerns may already be reflected in stock prices. The question now is whether improving growth can provide a trigger for these multiples to recover.
Street remains firmly positive
Street sentiment also remains strong despite the stock-price weakness.

SBI Life has 38 buy calls, one hold and no sell recommendations. HDFC Life has 37 buys, one hold and no sells. ICICI Prudential Life has 32 buys and five holds, with no sell calls. LIC has 22 buys, two holds and one sell.
This suggested that the recent underperformance has not materially dented the Street's longer-term confidence in the sector.
August data shows a clear pickup
The latest premium data adds weight to the recovery argument.
Life insurers' new business premium jumped 33.1% year-on-year to Rs 41,198 crore in August, compared with 20% growth in July. On a year-to-date basis, new business premium was up 20.4%.

LIC led the growth, with new business premium rising 45.3%, while private insurers grew nearly 20%. Among listed private players, HDFC Life's new business premium rose around 18%, while Bajaj Life grew around 32%.

Individual WRP growth also improved to around 14% in August, with private insurers growing around 15%. SBI Life led the listed private insurers on this metric with around 22% growth, followed by HDFC Life at 17% and ICICI Prudential Life at 11%.
Q1 earnings provide another positive
The improving premium trend comes on the back of resilient Q1 FY27 earnings, with insurers benefiting from a greater focus on higher-margin non-participating and protection products.
LIC's profit rose 22.8% year-on-year to Rs 13,492 crore, while VNB jumped 61.3% to Rs 3,136 crore. Its VNB margin expanded to 22.9% from 15.4% a year earlier.
ICICI Prudential Life's profit increased 27.8% to Rs 386 crore, while VNB rose 24.9% to Rs 571 crore. Its VNB margin expanded to 26.9%.
SBI Life reported a 22% rise in profit to ₹725 crore, with VNB up 29% to Rs 1,410 crore. Its VNB margin stood at 26.2%.

HDFC Life's reported VNB margin was 25%, but the company said it would have been 25.6% without the impact of GST restructuring. It also said underlying profit growth would have been 17% instead of the reported 12%.

Taken together, the picture is improving: premium growth is picking up, earnings remain resilient and valuations have corrected. The next leg for insurance stocks, however, will depend on whether the August momentum sustains and translates into stronger retail growth and margins.

title: Insurance stocks: Premium growth picks up in August, is there a re-rating ahead?
